learning_outcomes.text: Effective use of information sources and resources of communication and assisted professional training (Internet portals, specialized software applications, databases, online courses, etc.) both in Romanian and in a language of international circulation.
Transmission of knowledge in order to help students acquire and develop effective communication skills.
Understanding the purpose, objectives and roles of professional communication.
Development of oral, direct or mediated communication skills: developing a speech, organizing and leading meetings, briefings, training seminars.
Development and/or improvement of written communication skills.
Development of skills based on which one can prepare specific documents: notes, circulars, memorandum, report, letter, business plan, writing a scientific report and a bachelor's thesis.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Defining communication. Factors involved in communication: the message, the sender and the receiver of information.
Active listening. The concept of active listening. The role of feedback in communication. Other factors that determine the success or failure of communication.

Non-verbal communication: characteristics and functions. Types of non-verbal communication: mime gesture, posture, tactile communication, clothing. The link between verbal and non-verbal means of communication.
Oral verbal communication (Part 1). The speech. Preparation of the speech. Issues related to audience structure and audience responsiveness. The relationship between the speaker and the audience.

Oral verbal communication (Part 2) Speech (continued). Writing the speech. The structure of a speech: the beginning of the speech, the introduction of the speech, the content of the speech, the conclusion. Elements of style in developing and delivering a speech.

Oral Verbal Communication (2) Speech (continued). Controlling emotions while giving a speech. Managing the time allocated to the speech. The role of non-verbal communication in the presentation of a speech.

Verbal communication (4). The interview as a form of communication within the organization. Types of questions specific to interviews within the organization. Methods of answering questions during an interview.
Written communication (1). Official correspondence. The components of an official letter: layout and format. The specific language of official letters. Types of official letters.
Written communication (2). The memorandum. Presentation. Types of memorandums. Format and content of a memorandum. Examples.
Written communication (3). Writing a scientific report and a bachelor's thesis.
Written communication (4). The report. Types of reports. Format and component parts of a report. Examples.

Written communication (5). Means of online communication. Electronic mail: advantages and disadvantages. Electronic messages: Vocabulary specific to the Internet and information technology. Writing an e-mail. Drafting and sending a fax.
Written communication (6). Writing a Curriculum Vitae. Types of curriculum vitae.
Written communication (7). Writing a cover letter. Format of a cover letter. Examples of cover letters.
assessment_rules: The minimum required condition for passing the exam (mark 5) is to know the fundamental notions required in the subjects without presenting details. For a mark of 10, thorough knowledge of all subjects is required. Students are required to answer several course-related questions to test their acquired knowledge.
